name: Banff
dek: The town composite. This is a destination sheet, not a national-park guide.
paragraphs: Banff in the 1991–2020 normals is the town composite. Member stations in the inventory are between 1,383.7 and 1,396.9 metres. This page is the town's climate and the Canadian practical facts. It does not list park fees, permits, or trails. That work lives elsewhere.

Rainfall and precipitation are both shown because they are not the same element. A winter month can look almost dry in the rainfall column and still carry precipitation as snow. No Banff tourism page we opened stated a tipping percentage, so none is printed. Calgary's figure is on the Calgary sheet and is not copied here.

climate.caption: Station composite: Banff, about 1,384–1,397 m. The town, not a park-wide average.
climate.elevation: 1,383.7–1,396.9 m across stations in the composite
climate.note: Environment and Climate Change Canada 1991–2020 climate normals for this composite station. Rainfall is the rainfall element. Precipitation, which includes the water equivalent of snow, is the second water column. Quality codes: maximum temperature A, rainfall D, precipitation C.

driving.label: Driving side
driving.detail: The Government of Canada's settling-in page says you must drive on the right-hand side of the road. It also says traffic laws are generally similar across the country and that some rules vary by province or territory.
driving.sourceTitle: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada, Driving in Canada

water.label: Tap water
water.detail: CDC's traveler page for Canada, last reviewed 8 October 2026, does not say whether tap water is safe or unsafe. It says food and water standards vary by destination and by what you are doing, and it points readers to CDC's food and water precautions. This page does not turn that into medical advice.

currency.label: Currency
currency.detail: ISO 4217 lists the currency name Canadian Dollar and the code CAD for Canada.

timeZone.label: Time zone
timeZone.detail: Banff is in Alberta. IANA's America/Edmonton comment covers Alberta. The CST abbreviation in that comment is not printed. The zone name is.
